Here’s a curated list of 15 standout restaurants in New York City for 2024, based on the latest rankings, awards, and reviews from sources like The New York Times, Michelin Guide, Eater NY, and Resy. I’ve included a mix of fine dining, casual gems, and trendsetting spots across neighborhoods and cuisines.
🏆 Top Tier & Michelin-Starred
Le Bernardin
Cuisine: French (seafood-focused)
Rating: ★★★ (Michelin), 4.8/5 (Google)
Price: $$$$ ($210+ for tasting menus)
Address: 155 W 51st St, Midtown
Why? Named #1 restaurant in the U.S. by La Liste for 3 years running. Elegant, flawless seafood dishes like tasting of raw fish and lobster tail.
Note: Reservations essential (book 2+ months ahead).
Jungsik New York
Cuisine: Modern Korean
Rating: ★★★ (Michelin)
Price: $$$$ ($295+ for tasting menu)
Address: 2 Harrison St, TriBeCa
Why? First Korean restaurant in the U.S. to earn 3 Michelin stars. Innovative dishes like fermented soybean pasta and Korean beef with black garlic.
Eleven Madison Park
Cuisine: Plant-based fine dining
Rating: ★★★ (Michelin), 4.7/5
Price: $$$$ ($335+ for tasting menu)
Address: 11 Madison Ave, Flatiron
Why? Legendary service and a 100% vegan menu (since 2021). The celery root cooked in a salt crust is iconic.
Atomix
Cuisine: Korean-American (tasting menu)
Rating: ★★ (Michelin), 4.8/5
Price: $$$$ ($265+ per person)
Address: 104 1st Ave, East Village
Why? Intimate (8 seats), 2 Michelin stars, and a 10-course journey blending Korean flavors with global techniques.
Per Se
Cuisine: French-American
Rating: ★★★ (Michelin), 4.7/5
Price: $$$$ ($355+ for tasting menu)
Address: 4 Columbus Circle, Time Warner Center
Why? Thomas Keller’s NYC outpost. 9-course tasting menus with wine pairings, overlooking Central Park.
🌟 2024 Award Winners & Buzzworthy
Le Veau d’Or
Cuisine: French (classic)
Rating: 4.6/5
Price: $$$ ($125 prix-fixe)
Address: 129 E 60th St, Upper East Side
Why? Eater NY’s "Best Comeback 2024"—revived after a long hiatus with a prix-fixe menuhonoring its 1960s legacy.
Corima
Cuisine: Northern Mexican (modern)
Rating: 4.7/5
Price: $$ ($60–$100)
Address: 58 E 7th St, East Village
Why? Resy’s 2024 Hit List for its tortillas made from heirloom corn and recado negro butter. À la carte or tasting menu.
Sawa
Cuisine: Lebanese (innovative)
Rating: 4.6/5
Price: $$$ ($80–$120)
Address: 109 Atlantic Ave, Brooklyn
Why? Resy’s 2024 pick for surprising, cross-cultural dishes like lamb neck with cherry molasses.
Penny
Cuisine: Seafood (casual-chic)
Rating: 4.5/5
Price: $$ ($50–$80)
Address: 129 E 7th St, East Village
Why? Resy’s "New Classic"—focused on sustainable seafood and a raw bar with creative small plates.
Carnitas Ramirez
Cuisine: Mexican (taqueria)
Rating: 4.7/5
Price: $ ($10–$20)
Address: 134 Ave A, Alphabet City
Why? Eater NY’s "Best Counter-Service Spot 2024"—nose-to-tail tacos (try the al pastoror birria).
🍽️ Neighborhood Gems
Via Carota
Cuisine: Italian (West Village)
Rating: 4.7/5
Price: $$ ($30–$60)
Address: 51 Grove St, West Village
Why? NYT’s Top 100—famous for cacio e pepe and natural wines. No reservations; expect a wait.
OLIO E PIÙ
Cuisine: Italian (trattoria)
Rating: 4.7/5
Price: $$ ($25–$50)
Address: 3 Greenwich Ave, West Village
Why? Cozy spot with handmade pasta (try the bucatini all’amatriciana).
Manhatta
Cuisine: New American
Rating: 4.7/5
Price: $$$$ ($150+ for tasting menu)
Address: 28 Liberty St (60th floor), Financial District
Why? Stunning skyline views + seasonal tasting menus by chef Daniel Humm.
Au Cheval
Cuisine: American (diner-style)
Rating: 4.7/5
Price: $$ ($20–$40)
Address: 33 Cortlandt Alley, Financial District
Why? Chicago’s famous burger (double cheeseburger with egg) now in NYC.
Four Twenty Five on Park Avenue
Cuisine: New American (fine dining)
Rating: 4.6/5
Price: $$$$ ($188 for 6-course tasting)
Address: 425 Park Ave, Midtown
Why? Forbes’ pick for Jean-Georges Vongerichten’s best restaurant in years—elegant space and well-priced tasting menu.
📌 Quick Tips for Booking
Reservations: Use Resy, OpenTable, or the restaurant’s website. For Le Bernardin, Eleven Madison Park, or Per Se, book 2–3 months in advance.
Walk-ins: Try Via Carota, OLIO E PIÙ, or Au Cheval (arrive early).
Budget-friendly: Carnitas Ramirez, The Best Sichuan (4.8/5, $15–$30), or Momofuku Noodle Bar (4.5/5, $20–$40).
Splurge-worthy: Jungsik, Atomix, or Manhatta for a special occasion.

These picks are based on 2024 rankings, local guides, and critic reviews (e.g., The New York Times, Eater NY, West Side Rag).
🏆 Top 10 Restaurants on NYC’s West Side (2024)
1. Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi
Cuisine: American-Caribbean-Creole
Rating: ★★★★★ (NYT #1 in NYC’s 100 Best Restaurants 2024)
Price: $$$$ ($150+ per person)
Address: Lincoln Center, 10 Lincoln Center Plaza
Why? #1 restaurant in NYC (NYT 2024). Chef Kwame Onwuachi’s tasting menu blends Caribbean, Creole, and American flavors. Must-book weeks in advance.
2. Jean-Georges
Cuisine: French-American-Asian
Rating: ★★★★ (NYT #19, 2 Michelin stars)
Price: $$$$ ($185+ for tasting menu)
Address: 1 Central Park West (Columbus Circle)
Why? Iconic fine dining with seasonal dishes like young garlic soup and herb-crusted lamb. Stunning Central Park views.
3. Barney Greengrass
Cuisine: Jewish (Smoked Fish & Bagels)
Rating: ★★★★ (NYT #66, 4.5/5 Google)
Price: $$ ($20–$40)
Address: 541 Amsterdam Ave
Why? Upper West Side institution since 1908. Famous for lox, whitefish salad, and bagels with schmear. Cash only; expect a weekend wait.
4. Sushi Kaito
Cuisine: Japanese (Omakase Sushi)
Rating: 8.5/10 (The Infatuation)
Price: $$$ ($80–$120)
Address: 211 W 79th St
Why? Hidden gem for omakase-style sushi with fresh, high-quality fish. Reservations recommended.
5. Mama’s TOO!
Cuisine: Italian (Casual)
Rating: 8.8/10 (The Infatuation)
Price: $$ ($30–$60)
Address: 208 W 79th St
Why? UWS favorite for handmade pasta (try the cacio e pepe) and a lively atmosphere. Walk-ins accepted at the bar.
6. La Dinastia
Cuisine: Chinese (Sichuan & Cantonese)
Rating: 8.4/10 (The Infatuation)
Price: $$ ($40–$70)
Address: 217 W 72nd St
Why? Spicy Sichuan dishes like dan dan noodles and mapo tofu. No reservations; expect a wait.
7. Bánh
Cuisine: Vietnamese (Modern)
Rating: 8.3/10 (The Infatuation)
Price: $$ ($30–$50)
Address: 231 W 72nd St
Why? Bib Gourmand winner (Michelin) for pho, bánh mì, and crispy pork belly. Reservations on Resy.
8. The Consulate
Cuisine: Global (Rotating Menu)
Rating: 4.6/5 (Google)
Price: $$$ ($60–$100)
Address: 246 W 72nd St
Why? Eclectic menu featuring dishes from around the world. Cozy, romantic vibe.
9. Playa Betty’s
Cuisine: California-style (Beach Vibes)
Rating: 4.5/5 (Google)
Price: $$ ($30–$60)
Address: 320 Amsterdam Ave
Why? Bright, airy spot with avocado toast, fish tacos, and margaritas. Great for brunch or dinner.
10. Motorino
Cuisine: Italian (Neapolitan Pizza)
Rating: 4.5/5 (Google)
Price: $$ ($20–$40)
Address: 510 Columbus Ave
Why? Best pizza on the UWS—margherita and diavola pies with wood-fired crust. Walk-ins welcome.
📌 Quick Tips for Tonight
For Reservations:
Use Resy (resy.com) for Tatiana, Sushi Kaito, Bánh, or Mama’s TOO!.
Jean-Georges and The Consulate may have last-minute availability on OpenTable.

Barney Greengrass, La Dinastia, Motorino, and Playa Betty’s often accept walk-ins (arrive before 6:30 PM or after 8:30 PM).
Budget-Friendly:
Barney Greengrass, Motorino, or Mama’s TOO! (under $60 for 2).

Tatiana or Jean-Georges (fine dining experience).
